source.primary_witnesses: Aramaic DSS fragments (4Q201-4Q207; late 3rd c. BCE through 1st c. BCE) where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus (6th c. CE) where Aramaic absent; Ge'ez (medieval; the only complete witness) as fallback
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly conventions: Aramaic Imperial-Aramaic transliteration per Milik 1976 (ḥ ṣ ʿ ḫ); Greek SBL convention (η→ē, ω→ō, θ→th, etc., matching Matthew precedent); Ge'ez SBL Ge'ez convention (ḫ ḫ̣ ʾ ʿ ä for ä-vowel)
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Milik 1976 DJD apparatus + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia + original codicology
source.fetchedFrom: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch + Black 1985 Greek text + Charles 1912 Ge'ez PD + Knibb 1978 Ge'ez critical edition + Nickelsburg 2001 Hermeneia commentary
source.citation: Milik 1976 The Books of Enoch (Oxford); Black 1985 The Book of Enoch or 1 Enoch (SVTP 7, Leiden); Nickelsburg 2001 1 Enoch 1 Hermeneia; Charles 1912 The Book of Enoch (Oxford, PD); Knibb 1978 The Ethiopic Book of Enoch (Oxford); Tigchelaar-García Martínez 2000 DJD XXXVI; VanderKam 1984 Enoch and the Growth of an Apocalyptic Tradition.
source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 23 — FIRE OF THE WEST CHASING THE LUMINARIES — Aramaic 4Q204 1 viii partial (very fragmentary); Greek Akhmim 23:1-4 complete; Ge'ez full. Raguel as guide.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἀπῆλθον εἰς ἄλλον τόπον τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἔδειξέν μοι πρὸς δυσμὰς ὄρος πυρὸς ἀνάπτοντος, διώκοντος ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτός.
verses.translit: Kai ekeithen apēlthon eis allon topon tēs gēs, kai edeixen moi pros dysmas oros pyros anaptontos, diōkontos hēmeras kai nyktos.
verses.text_geez: ወእምህየ፡ ሖርኩ፡ ውስተ፡ ካልእ፡ መካን፡ ዘምድር፡ ወአርአየኒ፡ መንገለ፡ ዐረብ፡ ደብረ፡ እሳት፡ ዘይነድድ፡ ወይሰድድ፡ መዐልተ፡ ወሌሊተ፡
verses.notes: **A mountain of burning fire in the West, running day and night.** Cosmic-fire-mountain pursuing the luminaries. The 'pyric mountain of the west' is the engine of the sun's nightly transit. Cross-corpus: Mesopotamian gates of the western mountain where Shamash enters; Egyptian Duat-passage.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ ἐπορεύθην πρὸς αὐτό, καὶ εἶδον ἑπτὰ ὄρη ἔνδοξα, πάντα διαφόρους ἀλλήλων ἔχοντα.
verses.translit: Kai eporeuthēn pros auto, kai eidon hepta orē endoxa, panta diaphorous allēlōn echonta.
verses.text_geez: ወሖርኩ፡ ኀቤሁ፡ ወርእኩ፡ ሰብዐተ፡ አድባረ፡ ክቡራነ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ እንዘ፡ ይትሌለዩ፡ በበይናቲሆሙ፡
verses.notes: **Note:** Some manuscript witnesses transition into the seven-mountains scene of ch 24 here; chapter divisions are post-medieval. The Greek as edited by Black preserves only short content under ch 23 (vv. 1-4 — the fire of the West and Raguel exchange).

verses.text_greek: Καὶ ἠρώτησα τὸν ἄγγελον λέγων· Κύριέ μου, τί ἐστιν τὸ πῦρ τοῦτο τὸ μὴ ἀναπαυόμενον;
verses.translit: Kai ērōtēsa ton angelon legōn; Kyrie mou, ti estin to pyr touto to mē anapauomenon?
verses.text_geez: ወአሰአልክዎ፡ ለመልአክ፡ እንዘ፡ እብል፡ እግዚእየ፡ ምንት፡ ውእቱ፡ ዝእሳት፡ ዘኢያዐርፍ፡
verses.notes: Enoch's question — what is the unresting fire?

verses.text_greek: Τότε ἀπεκρίθη μοι Ῥαγουὴλ ὁ εἷς τῶν ἁγίων ἀγγέλων ὁ μετ' ἐμοῦ ὤν, καὶ εἶπέν μοι· Οὗτος ὁ δρόμος τοῦ πυρός, τοῦ διώκοντος πρὸς τὰ δυσμὰς πάντας τοὺς φωστῆρας τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.
verses.translit: Tote apekrithē moi Raguēl ho heis tōn hagiōn angelōn ho met' emou ōn, kai eipen moi; Houtos ho dromos tou pyros, tou diōkontos pros ta dysmas pantas tous phōstēras tou ouranou.
verses.text_geez: ወአውሥአኒ፡ ራጉኤል፡ አሐዱ፡ እመላእክት፡ ቅዱሳን፡ ዘምስሌየ፡ ሀሎ፡ ወይቤለኒ፡ ዝሩጸ፡ እሳት፡ ዘይሰድድ፡ መንገለ፡ ዐረብ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ ብርሃናተ፡ ሰማይ፡
verses.notes: **Raguel** (cf. 20:4 — over the world of luminaries) reveals: the fire chases all the luminaries of heaven westward. The fire is the cosmological engine of sunset / luminary-circuit. Picks up 17:4 (fire of the west receives the sun).
